subject.title: [Bug]: Ctrl+C not working in Windows install on foreground

question: Should this issue wait for native Windows npm-global Ctrl+C reproduction before any new fix PR is queued?
rationale: Current source already handles delivered SIGINT, so automation cannot safely choose a fix layer until a Windows-capable maintainer or reporter proves whether Ctrl+C is not delivered or shutdown stalls after delivery.

options.title: Require Windows live repro
options.body: Keep this issue open until PowerShell, cmd.exe, or Windows Terminal proof against current main or the latest package identifies the failing layer.

options.title: Queue after delivery proof
options.body: If live proof shows Ctrl+C is not delivered to the foreground process, queue a narrow keypress/wrapper repair with cleanup tests and Windows package proof.

options.title: Close if current Windows package passes
options.body: If a native Windows npm-global run on the latest package exits cleanly on Ctrl+C across common shells, close as cannot reproduce with that proof.

recommendation.title: Require Windows live repro
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until PowerShell, cmd.exe, or Windows Terminal proof against current main or the latest package identifies the failing layer.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to the most repeated work across Gateway CLI command and documentation surfaces, making this the best available routing owner for the proof sufficiency call.
